title: Control-to-Telemetry Mapper and Evidence Claim Automator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a system that maps formal control statements (SOC 2, ISO 27001) to concrete telemetry signals and produces cryptographically-signed evidence claims that can be ingested into the residency/retention evidence pipeline. The feature should: 1) provide a declarative mapping UI for PMs/auditors to link controls -> signals (logs, metrics, config snapshots), 2) run periodic collectors to assemble artifacts, 3) generate an immutable evidence claim (hash + signature + retention policy) and push to the evidence ledger and customer evidence bundles, and 4) expose coverage metrics and remediation tickets when signals are missing. This reduces manual evidence gathering during audit and supports cross-region retention constraints.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: aligned PM/Eng/SEC on scope. Decided to target top 25 controls used in our SOC 2 and ISO packages for MVP.
2026-03-03 - Design check-in (Morgan Chen): provided wireframes for the mapping UI and suggested inline examples for common signals (KMS rotates, audit log exports, VPC flow logs).
2026-03-05 - Eng sync (Rajat): agreed to reuse existing evidence harvester framework but emit new 'claim' artifacts rather than raw bundles. ENG will implement claim schema and signing endpoint.
2026-03-07 - Security review request submitted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Claim-Schema-Review. Requested threat modeling for claim signing keys and HSM/KMS usage.
2026-03-09 - QA note: need negative tests for partial telemetry (e.g., missing config snapshot) and verify that claim generation fails fast with clear remediation steps.
2026-03-10 - PM update: scope locked for MVP -> control mapping UI, claim generator, ledger push, coverage dashboard. Post-MVP: automated remediation playbooks and multi-tenant evidence views.
acceptance_criteria: UI: PM/auditor can create a mapping between a control (by id + description) and one or more telemetry sources within the console
Collectors: scheduled collectors capture required artifacts and produce intermediate artifacts (logs, snapshots, metric windows) into the staging bucket
Claim generation: system produces a signed evidence claim JSON containing: control id, artifact references (S3/GCS path), artifact hashes, region tag, retention policy, and signer metadata
Ledger ingestion: claim is written to the immutable evidence ledger and appears in customer evidence bundles for the corresponding region
Coverage dashboard: shows percentage coverage per control and flags missing telemetry with suggested remediation steps
Failure handling: missing or outdated telemetry triggers a remediation workflow that creates a ticket and annotates the claim as 'incomplete' (not allowed for final attestations)
Security: signing keys stored in KMS; signing operation audited and reviewed by security team
Docs: Confluence runbook describing mapping conventions, retention semantics, and audit playbook is published
implementation_steps: Design: finalize mapping UI mocks and inline examples (Design lead: Morgan Chen).
Schema: define EvidenceClaim schema v1 (fields: control_id, artifacts[], artifact_hashes[], region, retention_tier, signer_info, timestamp, claim_status)
Collectors: extend harvest agents to emit artifact metadata and compute SHA256 hashes
Signing: build claim-signing microservice that calls customer KMS/HSM or Redwood KMS based on deployment type
Ledger: adapt evidence-ledger ingestion API to accept Claim objects and enforce immutability and retention tags
Console: add coverage dashboard and mapping editor; wire to backend endpoints
E2E tests: simulate synthetic telemetry, generate claims, verify ledger entries, and run audit export
Runbook: document manual steps and failure modes; add playbooks for auditors to request missing artifacts
notes: Trade-offs: We could embed full artifacts into claims but that increases bundle size and retention complexity. Chose artifact references + hashes for MVP to keep ledger small and rely on the evidence store for heavy payloads.

Privacy/regional constraints: claims must include region tags; when artifacts live in a different region than the control asserts, the system must mark cross-region and apply retention exceptions or require regional copies.
Operational: claims are final only after a 24-hour hold window to allow last-minute collector retries; this mitigates transient telemetry delays
Future: plan to add automated remediation playbooks that can enable missing telemetry pipelines (e.g., enable VPC flow logs) via runbook-driven automation
